reason: Eight unconditional FastMCP tools implement read-only GA4 Data API reports/metadata and Admin API property discovery; stdio entrypoint resolves to the server main.

tools.name: ga4_list_properties
tools.description: List every GA4 property accessible with the current read-only credentials.
tools.behavior: Paginate Admin API accountSummaries with pageSize 200 and nextPageToken; flatten account and property summaries into account_id, account_name, property_id, property_name and property_type.

tools.name: ga4_overview
tools.description: Return daily users, sessions, engagement, key events, and revenue.
tools.behavior: Run historical report with date dimension and activeUsers, newUsers, sessions, engagedSessions, engagementRate, keyEvents and totalRevenue metrics, fixed limit 366; return flattened rows.
notes: Property IDs are stripped, accept a properties/ prefix, and must then be numeric; this restriction is enforced by the handler, not the exposed schema.
Reports fetch one page only; flattened output includes row counts, truncation warnings, metadata and quota. No automatic report pagination.

tools.name: ga4_top_pages
tools.description: Return top page paths and titles ordered by page views.
tools.behavior: Run historical report with pagePath/pageTitle dimensions and screenPageViews, activeUsers, sessions, engagementRate metrics, ordered by screenPageViews descending; return flattened rows.
notes: Property IDs are stripped, accept a properties/ prefix, and must then be numeric; this restriction is enforced by the handler, not the exposed schema.
Reports fetch one page only; flattened output includes row counts, truncation warnings, metadata and quota. No automatic report pagination.
Handler enforces limit between 1 and 10000; no bounds are declared in the exposed schema.

tools.name: ga4_acquisition
tools.description: Return session channels and source/medium acquisition performance.
tools.behavior: Run historical report with sessionDefaultChannelGroup/sessionSourceMedium dimensions and sessions, activeUsers, engagedSessions, keyEvents metrics, ordered by sessions descending; return flattened rows.
notes: Property IDs are stripped, accept a properties/ prefix, and must then be numeric; this restriction is enforced by the handler, not the exposed schema.
Reports fetch one page only; flattened output includes row counts, truncation warnings, metadata and quota. No automatic report pagination.
Handler enforces limit between 1 and 10000; no bounds are declared in the exposed schema.

tools.name: ga4_events
tools.description: Return top GA4 events, users, key events, and event values.
tools.behavior: Run historical report with eventName dimension and eventCount, totalUsers, keyEvents, eventValue metrics, ordered by eventCount descending; return flattened rows.
notes: Property IDs are stripped, accept a properties/ prefix, and must then be numeric; this restriction is enforced by the handler, not the exposed schema.
Reports fetch one page only; flattened output includes row counts, truncation warnings, metadata and quota. No automatic report pagination.
Handler enforces limit between 1 and 10000; no bounds are declared in the exposed schema.

tools.name: ga4_run_report
tools.description: Run a custom historical GA4 report with requested dimensions and metrics.
tools.behavior: POST historical runReport with supplied dimensions, metrics and date range, stringified limit and returnPropertyQuota=true. Truthy arbitrary dimension_filter/metric_filter objects are forwarded directly as dimensionFilter/metricFilter. Optional metric ordering is applied; return flattened rows.
notes: Property IDs are stripped, accept a properties/ prefix, and must then be numeric; this restriction is enforced by the handler, not the exposed schema.
Reports fetch one page only; flattened output includes row counts, truncation warnings, metadata and quota. No automatic report pagination.

Handler strips/drops empty names, requires 1–9 dimensions and 1–10 metrics and validates names against `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*`. It enforces limit 1–10000 and order_by_metric membership in requested metrics; these restrictions are absent from exposed schema.

tools.name: ga4_realtime
tools.description: Run a GA4 realtime report for activity from the last 30 minutes.
tools.behavior: POST runRealtimeReport with supplied dimensions and metrics, stringified limit, returnPropertyQuota=true and optional metric ordering; return flattened rows.
notes: Property IDs are stripped, accept a properties/ prefix, and must then be numeric; this restriction is enforced by the handler, not the exposed schema.
Reports fetch one page only; flattened output includes row counts, truncation warnings, metadata and quota. No automatic report pagination.

Handler strips/drops empty names, requires 1–4 dimensions and 1–4 metrics and validates names against `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*`. It enforces limit 1–10000 and order_by_metric membership in requested metrics; these restrictions are absent from exposed schema.

tools.name: ga4_metadata
tools.description: List compatible GA4 dimensions and metrics, optionally filtered by text.
tools.behavior: GET property metadata. If search is truthy, case-insensitively filter dimensions and metrics by combined apiName, uiName, description and category text. Append propertyId and return metadata.
notes: Property IDs are stripped, accept a properties/ prefix, and must then be numeric; this restriction is enforced by the handler, not the exposed schema.
Despite description saying compatible dimensions and metrics, this calls getMetadata only; no checkCompatibility request is made.
Source review only, no tools/list or live requests.
No .git directory exists; supplied revision is authoritative.
All eight registrations are unconditional. CLI auth/config commands are not MCP tools.

Credentials load lazily from GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, local ga4-cli/google-credentials.json or Google ADC with analytics.readonly scope. Python >=3.11 and declared google-auth, mcp and requests dependencies are required; no definite entrypoint blocker found.

review.method: Independently compared all eight Python signatures, defaults and full docstrings; read every decorated handler, preset request, paginated property discovery and native REST report/realtime client validation. Distinguished handler-only limits from the emitted schema.
